# s5x command reference

<!-- GENERATED by cli/gen_skill_ref.ts from the CLI's own command tree.
     Do not edit by hand: cli/skill_test.ts fails when this file and the
     tree disagree. Change the verb, then run `bun cli/gen_skill_ref.ts`. -->

Every command and flag the `s5x` binary accepts. `sbx` is the same binary.

**Global flags.** `--json` and `--help` are valid anywhere before a `--`.
`--json` puts machine-readable output on stdout. A failed request is
`{"error", "status", "requestId", "retryAfter", "code", "exit", "sandbox",
"path", "sandboxes", "drive", "holders"}` (the fields that apply) and exits
1; a refused invocation (unknown command or option, missing or extra
argument) is `{"error", "detail"}` and exits 2. `--version` (or `-v`) works
only on its own, as the whole command after `s5x`.

## s5x sandbox

create and drive sandboxes

### `s5x sandbox create <ref> --template <template> [flags]`

create and boot a sandbox

- `<ref>` — your name for it, unique among your sandboxes
- `--template <value>` (required)
- `--vcpus <value>` — its vCPUs; 1 if left out. A sandbox is at most 4 vCPUs and 8192 MB
- `--mem <value>` — its memory in MB (at least 256); 2048 if left out. A size other than 1 vCPU / 2048 MB boots cold: seconds, not milliseconds
- `--env <value>` — KEY=VALUE, repeatable
- `--region <value>` — where to place it; omit for anywhere with capacity. A region s5x does not serve is refused with the list
- `--idle <value>` — seconds with nothing happening in it before it sleeps (default 30): no CPU work, no data in or out, no request of its own waiting on an answer, no call from you in flight. 0 never sleeps; otherwise at least 5
- `--ttl <value>` — delete it this long from now (24h, 7d), busy or not
- `--ttl-idle <value>` — delete it after this long without activity
- `--volume <value>` — name[:path], repeatable: a durable disk at path (/data if left out), at most 4; vsn_…:path, a snapshot, read-only, at most 4. Every one is mounted before its app starts
- `--create` — make every --volume you do not have yet, on the sandbox's machine
- `--allow-hosts <value>` — allow TCP 80/443 only to these hosts and header-rule hosts from the first boot, comma-separated exact names
- `--header <value>` — host:header[=value], repeatable: a header rule from the first boot; omit =value to be prompted

### `s5x sandbox ls`

your sandboxes

### `s5x sandbox rm <ref>`

destroy a sandbox; its name is free at once. Its volumes survive, detached, once its deletion finishes -- each a disk for another sandbox, which gets the disk and nothing else

- `<ref>` — the sandbox

### `s5x sandbox erase <ref>`

delete a sandbox and what it holds -- its vault and header rules, the read-write volumes it holds and their snapshots, its own snapshots, schedules, previews and logins, and every backup of it and of those volumes -- and say what it removed

- `<ref>` — the sandbox

### `s5x sandbox exec <ref> <cmd> [flags]`

run a command inside a sandbox and wait; its output is text, so copy files with `sandbox cp`

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<cmd>` — QUOTE it: one argument, not many
- `--timeout <value>` — seconds before it is killed (default 30, max 60)

### `s5x sandbox shell <ref>`

interactive shell inside a sandbox; exits with the shell's exit status. An open shell keeps the sandbox awake and pauses its --ttl-idle clock until it closes

- `<ref>` — the sandbox

### `s5x sandbox cp <src> <dst>`

copy a file in or out (ref:/path for the remote side)

- `<src>`
- `<dst>`

### `s5x sandbox stats <ref>`

resource use and request counts

- `<ref>` — the sandbox

### `s5x sandbox set <ref> [flags]`

change a sandbox's idle timeout, deadlines or size

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `--idle <value>` — seconds with nothing happening in it before it sleeps (default 30): no CPU work, no data in or out, no request of its own waiting on an answer, no call from you in flight. 0 never sleeps; otherwise at least 5
- `--ttl <value>` — delete it this long from now (24h, 7d), busy or not; or 'none'
- `--ttl-idle <value>` — delete after this long idle, or 'none'
- `--vcpus <value>` — its vCPUs: the same sandbox at a new size, at most 4 vCPUs and 8192 MB, its processes restarted at its next wake
- `--mem <value>` — its memory in MB (at least 256), as --vcpus
- `--now` — apply the size now: sleeps it if it is awake and boots it at the new size (its processes restart). Needed for one that never sleeps

### `s5x sandbox recover <ref> [flags]`

restart a dead sandbox on its own filesystem; s5x tries it at every wake, and a dead sandbox is kept until you recover or delete it. On a lost machine, once s5x has made sure it is off, a sandbox with no volume is moved and started fresh from its build

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `--force` — also restart one whose VM is up but not answering, ending every process in it

### `s5x sandbox promote <ref> <build> [flags]`

move this one sandbox to another build of its template, at its next wake or --now

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<build>` — the build `template show` lists: its digest, or its tpl_ id
- `--now` — switch now: reboots it on the new build (files outside the volume and `proc run` processes are lost). Normally refused while it holds a keep-alive

### `s5x sandbox proc run <ref> <cmd> [flags]`

start a detached process; survives sleep

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<cmd>` — quote it
- `--name <value>` — address it by this name instead of a generated one
- `--cwd <value>` — working directory
- `--timeout <value>` — seconds before it is killed; 0 never (default 600)
- `--keep-alive` — hold the sandbox awake while it runs
- `--env <value>` — KEY=VALUE, repeatable

### `s5x sandbox proc ls <ref>`

processes in a sandbox

- `<ref>` — the sandbox

### `s5x sandbox proc logs <ref> <name> [flags]`

output of a detached process

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<name>`
- `--stream <value>` — stdout | stderr | all (default all; stdout with --follow)
- `--follow` — keep printing one stream until the process exits

### `s5x sandbox proc kill <ref> <name> [flags]`

signal a process (SIGTERM, or SIGKILL with -9)

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<name>`
- `--force` — SIGKILL instead of SIGTERM (alias `-9`)

### `s5x sandbox proc restart <ref> <name>`

restart the sandbox's entrypoint, app (it starts again 2 s after it ends)

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<name>`

### `s5x sandbox schedule add <ref> <name> --exec <exec> [flags]`

create a schedule on a sandbox

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<name>` — unique on this sandbox
- `--cron <value>` — repeat: 5-field, @daily, or @every 15m -- UTC unless CRON_TZ=
- `--at <value>` — run once at this instant, RFC 3339 with its offset (2026-11-06T09:00:00+01:00)
- `--max-lateness <value>` — how late a run may still start, as 30m or 2h; past it the run is recorded too_late
- `--exec <value>` — the command to run in the sandbox (required)

### `s5x sandbox schedule ls <ref>`

schedules on a sandbox

- `<ref>` — the sandbox

### `s5x sandbox schedule rm <ref> <name>`

delete a schedule

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<name>`

### `s5x sandbox schedule run <ref> <name>`

run a schedule now; it starts at the next poll, within seconds

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<name>`

### `s5x sandbox schedule runs <ref> <name> [flags]`

recent occurrences of one schedule, newest first, each with how it ended

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<name>`
- `--limit <value>` — how many (default and most: 50)
- `--output` — include each run's output

### `s5x sandbox schedule set <ref> <name> [flags]`

change a schedule's cron or instant, command, lateness or enabled state

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<name>`
- `--cron <value>`
- `--at <value>`
- `--exec <value>`
- `--max-lateness <value>` — how late a run may still start, as 30m or 2h; none for the default
- `--enable`
- `--disable`

### `s5x sandbox vault login set <ref> [flags]`

create a login, or change one with --id; the password is a hidden prompt or piped stdin, never an argument

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `--website <value>` — a hostname such as github.com (www. is implied), repeatable, 1 to 10; required to create
- `--username <value>` — the username; "" is none
- `--hint <value>` — a note, not secret (up to 500 bytes)
- `--id <value>` — change this login (lg_...) and send only what the flags give; a new password is read only from piped stdin, and a pipe that never closes blocks
- `--totp-stdin` — stdin is the TOTP seed (otpauth:// URI or base32); on create the password is then prompted on a terminal
- `--remove-totp` — with --id: delete the stored TOTP seed

### `s5x sandbox vault login ls <ref>`

the logins -- websites, usernames and hints, never passwords or seeds

- `<ref>` — the sandbox

### `s5x sandbox vault login rm <ref> <id>`

delete one login

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<id>` — the login (lg_...)

### `s5x sandbox vault set <ref> <key> [value]`

seal a value into a sandbox's vault; omit the value to be prompted

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<key>`
- `[value]` — omit it (or pipe it in) to keep it out of your shell history

### `s5x sandbox vault get <ref> <key>`

read a value back

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<key>`

### `s5x sandbox vault ls <ref>`

what is in a vault -- names, never values

- `<ref>` — the sandbox

### `s5x sandbox vault rm <ref> <key>`

delete one value

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<key>`

### `s5x sandbox preview create <ref> [port] [flags]`

mint a preview URL

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `[port]` (default `80`)
- `--ttl <value>` — 1h, 24h, 7d; max 90d (default `24h`)

### `s5x sandbox preview ls <ref>`

a sandbox's preview URLs

- `<ref>` — the sandbox

### `s5x sandbox preview rm <ref> <id>`

revoke a preview URL

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<id>`

### `s5x sandbox snapshot create <ref> <name>`

checkpoint a sandbox under a name, and wait until it is taken (replaces a snapshot already under that name)

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<name>`

### `s5x sandbox snapshot ls <ref>`

checkpoints of a sandbox

- `<ref>` — the sandbox

### `s5x sandbox snapshot restore <ref> <name>`

put a checkpoint back, and wait until it is done: memory, processes and disks (env, vault, network, schedules and URLs are unchanged)

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<name>`

### `s5x sandbox snapshot rm <ref> <name>`

delete a checkpoint

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<name>`

### `s5x sandbox backup create <ref> [flags]`

back a sandbox up to s5x object storage -- its machine and every volume it holds -- and wait until the backup is taken (nothing is downloaded). One volume alone is `s5x volume backup`

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `--no-wait` — answer at once; the backup carries on

### `s5x sandbox backup show <id>`

one backup by its id; one still being taken, or one that failed, is `s5x operation show <id>`

- `<id>`

### `s5x sandbox backup ls [ref]`

backups of a sandbox, newest first; without one, all of yours, a deleted sandbox's and a volume's too. A volume's are `s5x volume backups`; ones still being taken are `s5x operation ls --kind backup --unfinished`

- `[ref]` — the sandbox

### `s5x sandbox backup restore <ref> <id>`

put a backup back, and wait until it is done. A machine backup restores memory, processes and every volume at its saved build and size, and the sandbox must hold the volumes it held then. A volume-only backup replaces that volume alone. The ref and URLs stay, and env, vault, network and schedules are unchanged. On a lost machine, once s5x has made sure it is off, a machine backup brings the sandbox back on another, and a volume-only one is refused. One volume of either alone, as a new volume, is `s5x volume restore`

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<id>`

### `s5x sandbox backup rm <id>`

delete a backup by its id (see `backup ls`)

- `<id>`

### `s5x sandbox env set <ref> <name> [value]`

create or replace a variable; omit the value to be prompted

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<name>`
- `[value]` — omit it (or pipe it in) to keep it out of your shell history

### `s5x sandbox env ls <ref>`

names, never values

- `<ref>` — the sandbox

### `s5x sandbox env rm <ref> <name>`

delete a variable

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<name>`

### `s5x sandbox network header set <ref> <host> <name> [value]`

set a header on HTTPS requests to one exact host on port 443; omit the value to be prompted

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<host>` — api.anthropic.com
- `<name>` — x-api-key, Authorization, ...
- `[value]` — omit it (or pipe it in) to keep it out of your shell history

### `s5x sandbox network header rm <ref> <host> <name>`

stop setting a header

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<host>`
- `<name>`

### `s5x sandbox network allow <ref> [hosts] [flags]`

allow HTTP(S), TCP 80/443, only to these hosts and header-rule hosts (exact names, comma-separated); --all lifts it, --none allows only header-rule hosts

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `[hosts]` — api.github.com,api.openai.com
- `--all` — anywhere: remove the allowlist
- `--none` — no host but its header-rule hosts (DNS still resolves)

### `s5x sandbox network ls <ref>`

its header rules (names, never values) and the hosts it may reach

- `<ref>` — the sandbox

## s5x template

docker images become templates

### `s5x template push <image> --name <name> [flags]`

upload a local image (at most 5 GiB compressed), make it a template, and wait until it is ready

- `<image>` — a local docker image tag
- `--name <value>` — template name (required)
- `--trusted-users <value>` — the users inside its sandboxes that may call their trusted routes, e.g. app,@staff (root always may; left out: as the last build; "" clears the list)

### `s5x template build <image> --name <name> [flags]`

make a template from an image in a public registry, and wait until it is ready

- `<image>` — a public image reference, e.g. oven/bun:1-alpine
- `--name <value>` — template name (required)
- `--trusted-users <value>` — the users inside its sandboxes that may call their trusted routes, e.g. app,@staff (root always may; left out: as the last build; "" clears the list)

### `s5x template ls`

templates

### `s5x template show <name>`

every build of one template, how many sandboxes run each, and why any failed

- `<name>`

### `s5x template promote <name> <build>`

move every sandbox of the template to a build, at its next wake, and make it the one new sandboxes get. Also the rollback

- `<name>`
- `<build>` — the build `template show` lists: its digest, or its tpl_ id

### `s5x template rm <name> <build>`

delete one build and its disk; refused while a sandbox, snapshot or backup uses it

- `<name>`
- `<build>` — the build `template show` lists: its digest, or its tpl_ id

## s5x volume

durable disks that outlive the sandboxes they are attached to, and grow as they fill

### `s5x volume ls`

your volumes, attached or not

### `s5x volume info <name>`

one volume: what it holds, where it is attached, how long its backups are kept

- `<name>` — the volume's name, or its vol_ id

### `s5x volume set <name> --backup-days <backup-days>`

how long its automatic backups are kept

- `<name>` — the volume's name, or its vol_ id
- `--backup-days <value>` — days automatic backups are kept (at most 30); its newest stays until a newer one replaces it; 0 takes none. A volume is backed up once a day, attached or not, encrypted, never sleeping or waking its sandbox, skipping a day it stayed detached or its sandbox stayed asleep or dead (required)

### `s5x volume rm <name>`

delete a detached volume, its data and its snapshots

- `<name>` — the volume's name, or its vol_ id

### `s5x volume attach <ref> <volume> [flags]`

attach a volume, or a snapshot read-only, to a sandbox, awake or asleep; its app sees it mounted when this answers

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<volume>` — name[:path], a volume at path (/data if left out), or vsn_…:path, a snapshot, read-only
- `--create` — make the volume, on the sandbox's machine, if you do not have it yet

### `s5x volume detach <ref> <path> [flags]`

unmount what is attached at a path, and free it; refused while processes hold it, unless --force

- `<ref>` — the sandbox
- `<path>` — where it is attached
- `--force <value>` — kill: kill the processes holding it first; restart: restart the sandbox without it (its processes restart), awake, asleep or dead

### `s5x volume snapshot take <name>`

snapshot a volume: attached, its writes are held for the instant of the copy; detached, it must have been unmounted cleanly

- `<name>` — the volume's name, or its vol_ id

### `s5x volume snapshot ls <name>`

a volume's snapshots, newest first

- `<name>` — the volume's name, or its vol_ id

### `s5x volume snapshot rm <name> <id>`

delete a snapshot no sandbox holds

- `<name>` — the volume's name, or its vol_ id
- `<id>` — the snapshot's vsn_ id

### `s5x volume fork <snapshot> <name>`

a new volume from a snapshot, on its machine, at once: it shares the snapshot's blocks until it is written

- `<snapshot>` — the snapshot's vsn_ id
- `<name>` — the new volume's name

### `s5x volume backup <name>`

back a volume up alone, attached or not, and wait until the backup is taken: its sandbox is never slept, only paused for the copy

- `<name>` — the volume's name, or its vol_ id

### `s5x volume backups <name>`

a volume's backups, newest first: its own, and the sandbox backups that hold it

- `<name>` — the volume's name, or its vol_ id

### `s5x volume restore <backup> <name> [flags]`

make a NEW volume of a backup's, and wait until it is done: a disk and nothing else, so a sandbox created on it is a new sandbox. --replace puts it back over its own volume instead

- `<backup>` — the backup's id (see `volume backups`)
- `<name>` — the new volume's name; with --replace, the backup's own volume
- `--drive <value>` — which volume of a sandbox's backup: rw0 (the default) to rw3
- `--next-to <value>` — put it on this sandbox's machine, so it can be attached there
- `--replace` — put the backup back over the volume it was taken of: what was written since is lost, and an attached one's sandbox boots cold at its next wake
- `--region <value>` — where to put it; any region with room if left out
- `--no-wait` — answer at once; the restore carries on

## s5x endpoint

a stable URL that survives the sandbox behind it

### `s5x endpoint create <name> <ref> [port] [flags]`

publish a hostname pointing at a sandbox

- `<name>`
- `<ref>`
- `[port]` (default `80`)
- `--public` — no token -- for webhooks that carry their own signature

### `s5x endpoint ls`

endpoints

### `s5x endpoint point <name> <ref>`

aim an endpoint at a different sandbox; takes effect within about 5 s

- `<name>`
- `<ref>`

### `s5x endpoint rm <name>`

delete an endpoint, its URL and its domains; they stop answering within about 5 s

- `<name>`

### `s5x endpoint domain add <endpoint> <domain>`

serve an endpoint at a domain of yours too; prints the CNAME record to add at its DNS provider

- `<endpoint>` — the endpoint's name (see `endpoint ls`)
- `<domain>` — the domain, such as bot.example.com

### `s5x endpoint domain ls`

your domains, their endpoints and states

### `s5x endpoint domain check <domain>`

look for a domain's CNAME now, restarting a failed one, and print where it stands; exits 0 once it is active, 1 while it is on its way, 2 when it failed and needs a fix

- `<domain>` — the domain, such as bot.example.com

### `s5x endpoint domain rm <domain>`

stop serving a domain; within about 5 s it no longer reaches the endpoint

- `<domain>` — the domain, such as bot.example.com

## s5x operation

backups, restores, snapshots, uploads and erases carried on for you, by id

### `s5x operation show <id>`

one operation: where it is, or why it failed (kept a day after it finishes)

- `<id>` — the operation's id: bk_…, rs_…, snp_…, upl_… or er_…

### `s5x operation wait <id>`

wait until an operation is done; Ctrl-C stops the wait, not the operation

- `<id>` — the operation's id: bk_…, rs_…, snp_…, upl_… or er_…

### `s5x operation ls [flags]`

your operations, newest first

- `--kind <value>` — only one kind: backup, restore, snapshot, upload or erase
- `--unfinished` — only the ones still under way
- `--failed` — only the ones that failed
- `--limit <value>` — how many, newest first (default 100, most 1000)

## s5x usage

what your sandboxes are consuming

### `s5x usage`

what your sandboxes are consuming

## s5x update

replace this binary, and its skills, with the current release

### `s5x update [flags]`

replace this binary, and its skills, with the current release

- `--check` — report what is available and change nothing
- `--force` — reinstall even if the versions match

## s5x skills

the skills that teach coding agents s5x, in ~/.agents/skills

### `s5x skills install`

write this release's skills into ~/.agents/skills and link them from ~/.claude/skills

### `s5x skills uninstall`

remove the s5x skills from ~/.agents/skills and ~/.claude/skills

## s5x logs

what happened to a sandbox, including deleted ones

### `s5x logs [ref] [flags]`

what happened to a sandbox, including deleted ones

- `[ref]` — sandbox name or id
- `--source <value>` — process | access | audit | system (default: records, or process if --proc/--stream is given)
- `--since <value>` — how far back, e.g. 30m, 2h, 1d (records only)
- `--until <value>` — stop this long ago (records only)
- `--level <value>` — warn | error -- and above (records only)
- `--grep <value>` — case-insensitive substring (records only)
- `--proc <value>` — which process (default `app`, your entrypoint; `console` is the VM's own serial output)
- `--stream <value>` — stdout | stderr | all (process only)
- `--lines <value>` — how many to show, at most 10000 records (default: the newest 1000 records, or up to the newest 256 KiB of each process stream)
- `--follow` — follow new output as it is written (alias `-f`)

### `s5x logs sandboxes [ref] [flags]`

what you still have logs for

- `[ref]` — only the sandboxes that had this name
- `--deleted` — only the ones that no longer exist

### `s5x logs stats [ref] [flags]`

how much there is, and how much of it is bad

- `[ref]`
- `--source <value>` — access | audit | system (default: all records; process output is bytes and is not counted -- read it with `s5x logs <ref> --source process`)
- `--since <value>` — how far back, e.g. 30m, 2h, 1d (records only)
- `--until <value>` — stop this long ago (records only)
- `--level <value>` — warn | error -- and above (records only)
- `--grep <value>` — case-insensitive substring (records only)

## s5x login

sign in through your browser, and store a key for this machine

### `s5x login [flags]`

sign in through your browser, and store a key for this machine

- `--no-browser` — the browser is on another machine (SSH, a container, a coding agent): print the link, take the code the page shows, or finish later with --code
- `--name <value>` — the name of this machine's key (default: its host name)
- `--code <value>` — finish a --no-browser sign-in with the code its page showed

## s5x logout

forget this machine's key, and revoke it if `s5x login` made it

### `s5x logout`

forget this machine's key, and revoke it if `s5x login` made it

## s5x whoami

whose API key this terminal is using, which key, and where it came from

### `s5x whoami`

whose API key this terminal is using, which key, and where it came from

## s5x key

API keys: make one for a server or CI job (S5X_API_KEY), list them, revoke one

### `s5x key create <name> [flags]`

make an API key for a server or CI job; you approve it in your browser and it is printed once

- `<name>` — the key's name, 1 to 64 printable ASCII characters
- `--no-browser` — the browser is on another machine: print the link, and take the code the page shows

### `s5x key ls`

the API keys `s5x key create` made (names and prefixes, never the keys); last used is to the hour

### `s5x key rm <id>`

revoke a key `s5x key create` made; whatever uses it is refused from its next request

- `<id>` — the key's id, key_…, as `s5x key ls` lists it

## s5x version

print the version

### `s5x version`

print the version
